newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy takes peace mission to Arafat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy takes peace mission to Arafat.

text.p: A U.S. Middle East peace envoy met Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Sunday and Palestinians insisted the American's mission must not be limited to dealing with security concerns.
Special envoy Dennis Ross told reporters in Jerusalem earlier that U.S. President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright wanted him to focus on security questions.

"We cannot confine the talks to security issues. This means we will have no talks at all because security is part of the overall peace process," Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo told Reuters before Arafat met Ross in self-ruled Ramallah.

"This is the Palestinian leadership's decision -- that all issues should be discussed with Ross in order to reach positive results," Abed Rabbo said, underscoring the hardships facing the envoy's mission.

The United States sent Ross to the Middle East to ease tensions plunged deeper into crisis by a July 30 suicide bombing at an Israeli market that killed 15 people including two Islamic suicide bombers. Ross met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem before going to Ramallah.

Arafat wants Israel to ease a security clampdown on Palestinians. Israel closed off the West Bank and Gaza after the market attack and conditioned any resumption of talks on Arafat cracking down on Islamic militant groups.
